definitions.explanation: The quality that makes something interesting or appealing; an attractive or engaging character.

examples.japanese: {興趣|きょうしゅ}に{富|と}んだ{話|はなし}だった。
{旅|たび}に{興趣|きょうしゅ}を{添|そ}える{出会|であ}いがあった。
examples.english: There were encounters that added charm to the journey.

examples.japanese: {興趣|きょうしゅ}を{感|かん}じさせる{展示|てんじ}だった。
examples.english: It was an exhibition that evoked interest.

notes:
{興趣|きょうしゅ} describes the quality of being interesting or appealing.

WORD FORMATION:
- {興|きょう} (interest, excitement) + {趣|しゅ} (charm, taste)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {興趣|きょうしゅ}に{富|と}む: to be rich in interest
- {興趣|きょうしゅ}を{添|そ}える: to add flavor/interest
- {興趣|きょうしゅ}を{感|かん}じる: to feel interest/charm
- {興趣|きょうしゅ}{深|ぶか}い: deeply interesting

USAGE NOTE:
{興趣|きょうしゅ} is a literary/formal word. In everyday speech, {面白|おもしろ}い or {興味深|きょうみぶか}い are more common.

RELATED WORDS:
- {趣|おもむき}: charm, flavor
- {趣味|しゅみ}: hobby, interest
- {興味|きょうみ}: interest (more common)
